bundles.evidenceText: out of nothing nothing comes and therefore something comes into being there surely has to be a cause that brings it into being.
bundles.rationale: The move defends the general causal principle for things that begin. No stated bridge isolates that premise, and one causal premise does not establish the complete pro motion bridge. The proposition can remain true while the actual-infinite, successive-addition, and personhood bridges fail, so no polarity applies and motion support is excluded.

bundles.evidenceText: We've never seen anything like that. I've no experience of that happening.
bundles.rationale: The move says ordinary rearrangements provide no experience-based support for causation of an absolute material beginning. That proposition can be true without changing the credibility of any stated finitude, successive-addition, Hilbert, or personhood bridge. No polarity applies; support for the con motion is excluded because the complete motion-level denial is not supplied.

bundles.evidenceText: every thing that begins to exist has a cause
bundles.rationale: The expressed proposition supports the universal causal premise and applies it to the universe. The packet states no separate causal-principle bridge, and contact with this one premise cannot inherit complete pro-motion status. It can be true while the past remains beginningless or personhood fails, so no polarity applies and pro-motion support is excluded.

bundles.evidenceText: that doesn't help. That doesn't explain why the universe
bundles.rationale: The move argues that paraphrasing claims about nothingness does not explain why a substance or universe must have a cause. This undercuts a defense of the causal premise, but no stated bridge represents that premise alone. The point can be true without affecting the listed infinite-past or personhood bridges, so no polarity applies and con-motion support is excluded.

bundles.evidenceText: there must have always been materiality one thing causing another in a descending chain turtles all the way down
bundles.rationale: The move affirmatively proposes an eternal, beginningless material chain. That directly supports the con central bridge that the Kalam fails to exclude a coherent beginningless material reality; if the proposition is true, that bridge becomes more credible. Pro-central attack is the nearest competitor, but the move advances the con alternative rather than directly analyzing the pro actual-infinite inference, and con-motion support is too broad.

bundles.evidenceText: it is impossible to form an actually infinite number of things by successive addition.
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that successive addition cannot form an actual infinite and applies this specifically to the past-event series. This supports the pro subsidiary-2 bridge; if true, its successive-addition inference is more credible. Pro-central support is excluded because the expressed reason contacts the narrower successive-addition bridge rather than independently establishing the entire central actual-infinite inference.

bundles.evidenceText: Hilbert said that the realm of infinite set theory
bundles.rationale: The move presents Hilbert’s fully occupied hotel and his restriction of infinite set theory to mathematical thought rather than reality. This supports the pro subsidiary-1 bridge that Hilbert-style concrete scenarios indicate metaphysical impossibility; if true, that bridge gains credibility. Pro-central support is excluded because the evidence contacts the narrower Hilbert bridge, not the entire temporal-series inference.

bundles.evidenceText: You can have proper parts that are equinumerous to the whole.
bundles.rationale: The move argues that equinumerosity between an infinite whole and a proper part is simply a feature of infinite collections and does not justify declaring them impossible. This directly attacks the pro subsidiary-1 Hilbert inference; if true, that inference loses credibility. Support for con subsidiary-1 is the nearest competitor, but the expressed force is a direct rebuttal of the pro bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: Give up the most controversial one that an actual infinite number of things can exist
bundles.rationale: The move argues that Hilbert-style cases warrant rejecting the real existence of actual infinities while retaining Euclid’s maxim and Hume’s principle. This supports the pro subsidiary-1 bridge; if the proposition is accepted, the claimed metaphysical impossibility becomes more credible. Pro-central support is excluded because the move supplies the narrower Hilbert-based reason rather than the whole past-finitude inference.

bundles.evidenceText: I don't see why I should make a big metaphysical concession when I could just change how I talk.
bundles.rationale: The move says the apparent inconsistent triad can be handled by using context-sensitive descriptions for infinite collections without conceding their metaphysical impossibility. This directly attacks the pro subsidiary-1 Hilbert inference; if true, that inference is less credible. Con-subsidiary support is excluded as the nearest competitor because the move is framed as a rebuttal to the pro bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: you can get any number from zero to infinity as result of these inverse operations.
bundles.rationale: The move claims that checkout operations on Hilbert’s Hotel yield incompatible remainders after subtracting identical infinite quantities, treating this as persuasive evidence against concrete actual infinities. This supports the pro subsidiary-1 bridge; if true, its metaphysical-impossibility claim gains credibility. Pro-central support is excluded because only the narrower Hilbert scenario is defended.

bundles.evidenceText: I get out the right answer, there's no contradiction.
bundles.rationale: The move argues that relative complements describe each hotel checkout case consistently and that the alleged contradiction comes from misleading pseudo-arithmetic. This directly attacks the pro subsidiary-1 claim that Hilbert-style cases reveal metaphysical impossibility; if true, that bridge is less credible. Con-subsidiary support is excluded as the nearest competitor because the move directly rebuts the pro argument.

bundles.evidenceText: you subtract in the normal sense of that word identical quantities from identical quantities and you get non-identical remainders.
bundles.rationale: The move maintains that ordinary subtraction applied to the concrete hotel produces an arithmetic contradiction despite set-theoretic restrictions. This supports the pro subsidiary-1 bridge that Hilbert-style concrete scenarios reveal metaphysical impossibility; if true, that bridge is more credible. Pro-central support is excluded because the proposition concerns only the narrower Hilbert case.

bundles.evidenceText: I can't get to the end of the endless, but the countdown I can get to the end of the beginningless.
bundles.rationale: The move identifies an asymmetry between an endless upward count and a beginningless countdown that nevertheless has a present endpoint. This directly attacks the pro subsidiary-2 inference from successive addition; if true, that inference is less credible. Support for con subsidiary-2 is the nearest competitor, but the expressed force is a direct criticism of the pro bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: if he could finish by today, he should have finished by any point in the infinite past.
bundles.rationale: The move argues that a counter completing a beginningless countdown today should already have completed it at any earlier point, contradicting the hypothesis that he was then still counting. This supports the pro subsidiary-2 bridge; if true, the impossibility of completing such a successive series is more credible. Pro-central support is excluded because the countdown inference is the narrower bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: Him having an infinite amount of time prior to today just means he could have finished it by yesterday. It doesn't mean that he should have done or he would have done.
bundles.rationale: The move says Craig reverses the relevant conditional: infinite prior time permits but does not require earlier completion of the countdown. This directly attacks the pro subsidiary-2 countdown inference; if true, that bridge is less credible. Support for con subsidiary-2 is excluded as the nearest competitor because the proposition expressly diagnoses and rebuts the pro argument.

bundles.evidenceText: why does he finish just now rather than yesterday since an infinite number of seconds had already elapsed?
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that even a restricted principle of sufficient reason requires an explanation for why an infinite countdown ends now rather than earlier. This supports the pro subsidiary-2 bridge by reinforcing the claimed impossibility of a beginningless countdown reaching the present; if true, that bridge gains credibility. Pro-central support is excluded because the specific countdown bridge is narrower.

bundles.evidenceText: Well, cuz he was counting two yesterday. He counts at the rate of one number a day.
bundles.rationale: The move argues that the preceding count and fixed counting rate provide an adequate partial explanation of today’s completion, without an ultimate explanation. This directly attacks the pro subsidiary-2 countdown objection; if true, that objection is less credible. Support for con subsidiary-2 is the nearest competitor, but the move is expressly answering and undercutting the pro bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: why the man counting from infinity should finish this countdown today
bundles.rationale: The move argues that citing yesterday’s count does not resolve the contextually relevant mystery of why the beginningless countdown finishes today. This supports the pro subsidiary-2 bridge; if true, the claimed explanatory defect in completing a beginningless series is more credible. Pro-central support is excluded because the expressed proposition concerns the narrower countdown inference.

bundles.evidenceText: you cannot live past midnight and yet no Grim Reaper can strike you down.
bundles.rationale: The move presents the Grim Reaper construction as producing a logical contradiction from successively traversing a non-well-founded descending series. This supports the pro subsidiary-2 bridge; if true, the metaphysical impossibility of forming or completing such a series is more credible. Pro-central support is excluded because this is a specific successive-addition illustration.

bundles.evidenceText: what we've actually shown is that there's a point if we go back finitely far uh at which kind of metricated time all begins.
bundles.rationale: The move argues that the finitude arguments establish at most a beginning of metric time and leave a non-metric beginningless past available. This directly attacks the pro central inference from those arguments to the beginning of the whole temporal series and universe; if true, that bridge is less credible. Con-central support is the nearest competitor, but the move expressly limits the pro inference.

bundles.evidenceText: You've got to dissolve the geometric structure of the line to characterize this time.
bundles.rationale: The move argues that the proposed pre-metric time must also lack linear geometry and consequently resembles a timeless point rather than a genuine beginningless temporal alternative. This attacks the con central claim that a coherent beginningless-past alternative remains; if true, that alternative is less credible. Pro-central support is excluded because the move does not establish the actual-infinite premise of that bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: the indeterministic causation option looks basically just the same except without the personal aspect to it
bundles.rationale: The move argues that an impersonal indeterministic mechanism can originate the universe at a particular time and is relevantly similar to libertarian agent causation. This directly attacks the pro subsidiary-3 inference that a personal agent is required; if true, that bridge is less credible. Con-subsidiary-3 support is the nearest competitor, but the move expressly challenges the pro personhood inference.

bundles.evidenceText: it doesn't make sense to have a changeless personal uh agent
bundles.rationale: The move argues from the essentially dynamic character of consciousness that a changeless, disembodied personal mind is incoherent. This attacks a necessary premise of the pro subsidiary-3 personal-agent bridge; if true, that bridge is less credible. Con subsidiary-3 is excluded because the move does not propose an impersonal indeterministic origin, and motion attack is too broad.

bundles.evidenceText: there is no incoherence in the notion of a timeless person.
bundles.rationale: The move argues that the freezing illustration supports the coherence of unchanging consciousness and that a timeless person is possible. This supports a necessary premise of the pro subsidiary-3 bridge identifying a personal agent as the explanation of a first universe; if true, that bridge is more credible. Pro-motion support is excluded because the move contacts only the narrower personhood inference.
